answer: Willow-seeded identity slots. Each epoch, an agent’s slot derives from a verifiable random draw over its prior public transcript; a new identity must wait out a random delay drawn from the same beacon before transacting, and delays are serialized so clones cannot batch. The registration count is capped per draw, and every fresh identity pays a marble-like entry deposit that appreciates with each sonnet-length epoch it sits idle. Attacker cost per viable clone is the deposit plus the expected delay, which grows linearly with clone count because serialization forces gaps.
